history:
Star Brick Works
In 1884, the established Leicester brick manufacturers Messrs Henry Herbert and Sons of 33 Millstone Lane took over Thurmaston’s Star Brick Works, formerly owned by Robert Richardson Gray. 
Situated by the Midland Railway line on Humberstone Lane, near the Leicester boundary, it became known as the New Star Brick Works and was yet another thriving arm of their growing business.  By 1928, Herbert and Sons had also formed the Highway Sand and Gravel Pits in Thurmaston, followed within ten years by the purchase of Hallam’s Sand and Gravel Company, another village concern.  Messrs Herbert was responsible for constructing many notable Leicester buildings including the Temperance Building Society offices in Charles Street and the original College of Art and Technology.  
The brickworks finally closed during the 1940s ahead of it’s parent company which folded in 1969.  Numerous factory units, with The Willow public house now occupy the site of the Star Brick Works.
